title: Key ceremony: transcripts, their checks and their hashes
generator: packages/crypto/scripts/ceremony-vectors.py: an independent Python implementation (standard library only), with share-encryption-vectors.py's ML-KEM-768 (checked against Go's accumulated FIPS 203 vectors first) and ristretto255, and trustee-vectors.py's P-256 ECDSA, which reproduces RFC 6979 Appendix A.2.5 first. Every value is test data, never keys

transcripts.description: Every seat of a 3-of-4 panel takes part honestly; all four qualify.
The smallest panel, 2-of-2.
MAX_TRUSTEES: an 11-of-16 panel, 240 challenges.
Seat 4 sends nothing; the other three qualify, which meets k = 3.
Seat 2's proof of knowledge of x has z + 1 (its message is signed as sent).
Seat 3's signing-key signature is made by seat 1's signing key.
Seats 2 and 3 register the same DH key, each with a valid proof: both hold x, and both are excluded.
Seat 1 registers its own identity key as its per-election signing key.
Seat 4 copies seat 1's keys and proofs: the proofs bind seat 1, so seat 4 fails possession and seat 1 is unaffected.
Seat 4 registers seat 1's ML-KEM key with its own DH key and proofs, and can't decapsulate, so it answers its challenges wrongly. Seat 1 still qualifies: there is no duplicate rule for ek.
Seat 2 sends no challenges (and so no reveals).
Seat 3 sends no answers.
Seat 1 sends no reveals; its challenges count against no one.
Seat 2 reveals a μ for seat 1 that doesn't encapsulate to its challenge; seat 1, whose answer can't be checked, is unaffected.
Seat 4 answers seat 1's challenge with something other than its shared secret.
Seats 3 and 4 register the same per-election signing key, each with a valid signature: both hold it, and both are excluded.

Seat 2 registers seat 1's ek, relays seat 1's challenge to it back to seat 1 as its own challenge, copies seat 1's answer and reveals seat 1's μ. The pair in m makes the relayed challenge fail its reveal: seat 2 is disqualified, and one seat is below k = 2.

Corrupt seats 3 and 4 of a 2-of-4 panel: seat 4 registers seat 1's ek; seat 3 relays seat 1's challenge to seat 4, and seat 4 relays seat 2's, each to seat 1 as its own challenge. Seat 4 answers every challenge correctly, but both relayers fail their reveals, leaving the two honest seats.
Seats 3 and 4 both answer wrongly; two qualified seats are below k = 3.
Round 1 lists seat 2 before seat 1.
Seat 3's challenges are dropped from round 2 after the fact, but its reveals stay in round 4.
Seat 1 sends one challenge too few.
Seat 1's round-1 message is swapped for another it also signed; every later message signed over the round 1 it replaced.
A byte of seat 4's answers is changed after it signed.
The run identifier is changed: every message was signed under the original context.
